question: The idea of Directive Principles of State Policy was borrowed from:
solution:
The correct answer is Ireland.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Constitutional Provisions: **Part IV** of the Constitution of India **(Article 36–51) **contains the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP).
 
• They are borrowed from the **Constitution of Ireland**, which copied it from the **Spanish Constitution**.
 
• **Article 37 **of the Indian Constitution states the **application **of the Directive Principles.
 
• These principles aim at ensuring socio-economic justice to the people and establishing India as a welfare state whereas fundamental rights ensure political justice.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Borrowed Features of the Indian Constitution__:**

 
 
• **Irish Constitution** - Directive Principles of State Policy, Nomination of Rajya Sabha members & Method of the election of the President.
 
• **US Constitution** - Fundamental rights, Independent judiciary and judicial review, Impeachment of the President, Removal of Supreme Court and High Court judges & Post of Vice-President.
 
• **France Constitution** - Republic, Ideals of liberty, equality, and fraternity in the Preamble.
 
• **Britain (UK) Constitution** - Parliamentary government, Rule of Law, Legislative procedure, Single Citizenship, Cabinet system, Prerogative writs, Parliamentary privileges, Bicameralism.
